article.title: NFL EDGE Saturday Evening Brief
article.dek: Philadelphia has a new starting quarterback, the designations are final, and the board still has not flipped — your last check before Sunday.

items.headline: Lead: Philadelphia has a new starting quarterback — Joe Milton III makes his first start Sunday
paragraphs: The Eagles are making a quarterback change for Sunday's game against the Giants. Joe Milton III starts, his first career NFL start, and Tanner McKee goes back to the bench after losing all three of his starts. Jalen Hurts is out for the season with blood clots.

Milton joined Philadelphia off the Dallas practice squad less than a month ago. He brings mobility and a big arm, and he faces a Giants defense ranked third against the pass. The Giants are 3-point favorites, and the total has fallen to 38.5.
The rest of the quarterback picture stands. Shedeur Sanders starts for Cleveland at New Orleans, Drew Lock starts for Seattle against Arizona, and Carson Wentz starts for Minnesota on Monday night.
items.takeaway: Milton starts for Philadelphia on Sunday, his first career start — and Sanders, Lock and Wentz start as expected.

items.headline: The designation rundown: Skattebo doubtful, Shaheed out, the Eagles lose two receivers
paragraphs: Friday's final designations are in, and nothing new landed during Saturday. Giants running back Cam Skattebo is doubtful with a hamstring injury, so Devin Singletary is the next man up. Seattle receiver Rashid Shaheed is out with a knee injury.

Philadelphia is down two receivers for Milton's first start: DeVonta Smith and Dontayvion Wicks are both ruled out. San Francisco is down three: Mike Evans, Deebo Samuel and Christian Kirk are all out against Las Vegas.

The Jets get Breece Hall back after five games out, but Garrett Wilson stays out with a concussion. A.J. Brown misses a second straight game. The questionable names — Amon-Ra St. Brown, George Pickens, Jake Ferguson, Emeka Egbuka, Hunter Henry and Kyle Monangai — go down to Sunday's inactive lists, about 90 minutes before kickoff.
items.takeaway: Skattebo is doubtful, Shaheed, Smith, Wicks, Samuel, Wilson and Brown are out — and the questionable names resolve at Sunday's inactives, about 90 minutes before kickoff.

items.headline: Weather: still calm — no wind flags anywhere on Sunday
paragraphs: The final forecast is in, and it looks the same as this morning. No Week 9 game is flagged for wind. Every outdoor game sits under 15 mph of sustained wind. The strongest gusts are 21 mph in Washington and 20 mph in Chicago and New England.

Seattle has a slight chance of light rain, 20 percent, with gusts to 18 mph. Chicago kicks off at 50 degrees under a mostly clear sky. The Madrid game plays under a retractable roof, and Cleveland at New Orleans and Monday night's Bills-Vikings game are indoors.
items.takeaway: Sunday is calm: no game is flagged for wind, gusts top out at 21 mph in Washington, and the Madrid game plays under a roof.

sections.title: What It Means for NFL EDGE

items.headline: The board still has not flipped — no Week 9 cards, so Sunday still goes through Check
paragraphs: Read again after the evening refresh, the app board still shows Week 8, generated November 2. There are no Week 9 cards at all. It has not flipped, and it has not picked up any of the Sunday quarterback changes.

The quarterback fields are stale across the board. Philadelphia still lists Tanner McKee, but Joe Milton III starts on Sunday. Cleveland still lists Deshaun Watson, but Shedeur Sanders starts. Seattle still lists Sam Darnold, but he is out and Drew Lock starts. If you read a Sunday quarterback off this board, you are reading last week.

So there is still no Sunday card to read, and you should not force a pick out of a stale board. That is what Check is for. Tap Check, type in your book's line and price, and the app runs it back through the model and the evaluator and gives you a bet or no-bet verdict on your price.
items.takeaway: Board still shows Week 8 with no Week 9 cards, so Sunday's prices go through Check until the board flips.

items.headline: Learn the Game: closing line value — did you beat the market?
paragraphs: Closing line value is a simple check on whether your price was any good. Compare the line you bet with the line at kickoff. If you bet a team at -3 and the line closes at -4.5, you got closing line value. You bought the same bet cheaper than the market ended up charging.

Hypothetical example, clearly labeled as hypothetical: say you take the underdog at +7 on Saturday, and by kickoff the line has moved to +5.5. You hold a better number than anyone betting at kickoff. That does not mean your bet wins. It means you paid less for it than the closing price.

Why it matters: over a season, consistently beating the closing line is one of the few signs your process is finding real value. A single bet proves nothing, but a pattern of good numbers usually beats a pattern of bad ones.
items.takeaway: If your number is better than the closing line, you got closing line value — a good sign your price was sharp, even before the game is played.

items.headline: Saturday was quiet — the morning's lines held
paragraphs: Nothing moved during Saturday. The three lines the morning brief flagged are sitting in the same place tonight: the Giants are still -3 against Philadelphia, Dallas is still -4.5 at Indianapolis, and the Chiefs-Jets total is still around 48.5.

The week's real moves happened before this morning. Houston went from -3.5 to -5.5 against the Chargers. Arizona went from +11.5 to +8.5 at Seattle, and that total fell five points, from 44.5 to 39.5. The Packers-Patriots total fell three points to 44.5, the Bills-Vikings total fell to 44.0, and the Madrid total climbed to 52.5.

The app board has not picked up any of this yet, because it still shows Week 8. So if your book has one of these numbers and it looks good to you, run it through Check. Type in your book's line and price, and the app runs it back through the model and the evaluator and gives you a bet or no-bet verdict on your price.
items.takeaway: The morning's lines held all day — Giants -3, Cowboys -4.5, Chiefs total 48.5 — and the week's bigger moves were already in place before this morning.

items.headline: The designations are in — bet the good number now
paragraphs: The last real information before Sunday is in. The final designations landed Friday, and nothing new came Saturday. The only thing left is the inactive lists, about 90 minutes before kickoff, and by then the good numbers are usually gone.

So do not keep waiting for a better price that may never come. If your book has a Sunday number you like and Check says bet, bet it now. The one exception is a game where you are specifically waiting on a questionable name — St. Brown, Pickens, Ferguson, Egbuka, Henry or Monangai. There, the inactive list is a real pending event, and it is worth the wait.
A quick price reminder: -120 means every $1.20 you risk wins $1. The app sets your actual stake from your bankroll and how aggressive you want to be.
items.takeaway: The designations are in, so run your book's Sunday price through Check — if it says bet, bet the good number now.

evidence.fact: Philadelphia is starting Joe Milton III at quarterback on Sunday against the New York Giants, his first career NFL start; Tanner McKee is benched after going 0-3 in three starts. Jalen Hurts is out for the season with blood clots. The switch was reported Wednesday by ESPN's Adam Schefter and NFL Network's Mike Garafolo and confirmed by head coach Nick Sirianni on Friday. The other Week 9 quarterback calls stand: Shedeur Sanders starts for Cleveland, Drew Lock starts for Seattle, Carson Wentz starts for Minnesota on Monday night.
evidence.interpretation: A fourth backup quarterback starts this week, and he has been with the team less than a month; the Eagles also lose two wide receivers (see designations).
evidence.app_guidance: Do not trust a stale quarterback field for this game; run the Giants-Eagles price through Check.
